description: Blank sex is reported as its own group alongside the other sexes.

b.request: Calculate per-patient averages of PT and IGA−IGM difference from laboratory records matched by ID, compute the ratio of each patient's IGA−IGM average to the overall mean, then for each sex including blank sex as a separate group, report average PT, average IGA−IGM difference, and average ratio.
b.sql: WITH patient_lab_stats AS (SELECT ID, AVG(PT) as avg_pt, AVG(IGA - IGM) as avg_iga_igm_diff FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(IGA - IGM) as overall_mean FROM Laboratory), patient_with_ratio AS (SELECT pls.ID, pls.avg_pt, pls.avg_iga_igm_diff, pls.avg_iga_igm_diff / om.overall_mean as ratio FROM patient_lab_stats pls CROSS JOIN overall_mean om), patient_sex_data AS (SELECT COALESCE(p.SEX, 'blank') as sex, pwr.avg_pt, pwr.avg_iga_igm_diff, pwr.ratio FROM patient_with_ratio pwr LEFT JOIN Patient p ON pwr.ID = p.ID) SELECT sex, AVG(avg_pt) as average_pt, AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) as average_iga_igm_difference, AVG(ratio) as average_ratio FROM patient_sex_data GROUP BY sex ORDER BY sex
b.raw: Calculate per-patient averages of PT and IGA−IGM difference from laboratory records matched by ID, compute the ratio of each patient's IGA−IGM average to the overall mean, then for each sex including blank sex as a separate group, report average PT, average IGA−IGM difference, and average ratio.

a.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), compute for each patient (by ID and sex) the average prothrombin time (`PT`) and the average of `IGA` − `IGM` per record, ignoring missing values. Also compute the mean of that IGA−IGM average across all patients, and divide each patient's IGA−IGM average by this overall mean. Then break the patients down by sex, keeping patients whose `SEX` is blank (an empty string) as a separate group of their own. For each sex, report the sex, the average of the patients' average PT, the average of their IGA−IGM averages, and the average of their ratios to the overall mean.
a.sql: WITH patient_stats AS (SELECT p.ID, COALESCE(p.SEX, '') as SEX, AVG(l.PT) as avg_pt, AVG(CASE WHEN l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL THEN l.IGA - l.IGM ELSE NULL END) as avg_iga_minus_igm FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, COALESCE(p.SEX, '')), global_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) as global_avg_iga_minus_igm FROM patient_stats WHERE avg_iga_minus_igm IS NOT NULL), patient_with_ratio AS (SELECT ps.SEX, ps.avg_pt, ps.avg_iga_minus_igm, CASE WHEN ps.avg_iga_minus_igm IS NOT NULL AND gm.global_avg_iga_minus_igm IS NOT NULL THEN ps.avg_iga_minus_igm / NULLIF(gm.global_avg_iga_minus_igm, 0) ELSE NULL END as ratio_to_global_mean FROM patient_stats ps CROSS JOIN global_mean gm) SELECT SEX, AVG(avg_pt) as avg_pt_by_sex, AVG(avg_iga_minus_igm) as avg_iga_minus_igm_by_sex, AVG(ratio_to_global_mean) as avg_ratio_by_sex FROM patient_with_ratio GROUP BY SEX ORDER BY SEX

c.request: Matching laboratory records to their patient on `ID` (lab records with no matching patient are dropped), work out each patient's (by ID and sex) average prothrombin time (`PT`) and average `IGA` − `IGM` difference per record, ignoring missing values. Also work out how each patient's IGA−IGM average compares to the mean across all patients, as their average divided by that mean. Then break this down by sex: for each sex, give the average PT, the average IGA−IGM difference, and the average ratio to the overall mean. Blank sex is reported as its own group alongside the other sexes.
c.sql:
WITH patient_lab_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    AVG(l.PT) as avg_pt,
    AVG(l.IGA - l.IGM) as avg_iga_igm_diff
  FROM Patient p
  INNER JOIN Laboratory l ON p.ID = l.ID
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
overall_mean_iga_igm AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) as overall_mean
  FROM patient_lab_averages
),
patient_with_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.avg_pt,
    pa.avg_iga_igm_diff,
    pa.avg_iga_igm_diff / om.overall_mean as ratio_to_mean
  FROM patient_lab_averages pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean_iga_igm om
)
SELECT 
  SEX,
  AVG(avg_pt) as average_pt,
  AVG(avg_iga_igm_diff) as average_iga_igm_difference,
  AVG(ratio_to_mean) as average_ratio_to_overall_mean
FROM patient_with_ratios
GROUP BY SEX
ORDER BY SEX

d.request: For each sex value including NULL as a distinct group, calculate average PT, average per-patient IGA-IGM difference, and average per-patient ratio of IGA-IGM to overall mean IGA-IGM, using laboratory records joined to patients by ID.
d.sql:
WITH lab_data AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    l.PT,
    l.IGA,
    l.IGM,
    (l.IGA - l.IGM) AS iga_igm_diff
  FROM Laboratory l
  JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
  WHERE l.PT IS NOT NULL AND l.IGA IS NOT NULL AND l.IGM IS NOT NULL
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(iga_igm_diff) AS mean_diff
  FROM lab_data
),
patient_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    ld.SEX,
    ld.ID,
    AVG(ld.PT) AS patient_pt_avg,
    AVG(ld.iga_igm_diff) AS patient_diff
  FROM lab_data ld
  GROUP BY ld.SEX, ld.ID
),
patient_ratios AS (
  SELECT 
    ps.SEX,
    ps.ID,
    ps.patient_pt_avg,
    ps.patient_diff,
    ps.patient_diff / om.mean_diff AS patient_ratio
  FROM patient_stats ps
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
)
SELECT 
  SEX,
  AVG(patient_pt_avg) AS avg_pt,
  AVG(patient_diff) AS avg_iga_igm_diff,
  AVG(patient_ratio) AS avg_ratio
FROM patient_ratios
GROUP BY SEX
ORDER BY SEX
